correctness.rationale: For all sets C of six-bit words with every proper cyclic splice of every ordered pair (including self) excluded from C and aligned Hamming distance at least three, primitive-word reduction leaves exactly 54 candidates. Feasibility is hereditary under taking subsets. Independent lexicographic complete DFS visits precisely (1,54,814,3042,2480,324,16) feasible codes in sizes 0 through 6, no larger sizes. There are exactly 16 size-six codes in four orbits of four under global reversal and bit complement, each with distance multiset eight 3 and seven 4; actual optimal_codes.txt matched enumerated optimizers. This exhaustively proves a finite extremal theorem, not synchronization after substitution during loss of framing.

originality.rationale: Full text of Levenshtein (2004) on comma-free codes inspected through all 13 pages, particularly Secs. 2-4, discusses the classical cyclic upper bound, comma-free separation index, asymptotics and stronger overlap-free codes, not the binary length-six joint comma-free/distance-three equality classification. Golomb et al. 1958 established original comma-free bounds without minimum distance three. Resultary six-bit code searches retrieved different error models (single-grain, deletion, burst or cross-bifix-free), not this precise constraint. The combined finite extremum and complete optimizer orbit is not determined by these prior results.
residual_risks: Older tables of simultaneous comma-free and Hamming-distance codes, including unindexed theses or Russian literature, might include the same finite n=6 optimum.

value.rationale: Joint boundary synchronization and aligned single-substitution correction is a standard and motivated coding tradeoff. Exact n=6 optimum plus a complete, symmetry-reduced classification of all optimal codebooks is useful as a small-block benchmark and countercheck of coding bounds; natural finite parameter data can have independent value without infinite-length claims.
